svg.title: A page on 41
svg.desc: The two-scalar page on p = 41 with (lambda, mu) = (26, 14), g = 6, M = 8, t = 5, H = <6^8> = {1, 10, 16, 18, 37}. The 41 hubs of Z_41 sit on a circle with 0 at the top; each nonzero hub is tinted by its coset C_j = 6^j H (eight hues, j = 0..7). The matching A = {x, 26x} on C_0 u C_2 and {x, 14x} on C_4 u C_6 is drawn as gold chords, B = {x, 26x} on C_1 u C_3 and {x, 14x} on C_5 u C_7 as cyan chords (log_6 26 = 17 and log_6 14 = 25 are both 1 mod 8, so the coset step is s = 1 and this is the probe's own assignment). Their union, traced as one thin bright path, is a single 40-cycle: 1 -> 26 -> 20 -> 28 -> 31 -> 24 -> 8 -> 30 -> 10 -> 14 -> 36 -> 34 -> 23 -> 35 -> 39 -> 13 -> 18 -> 17 -> 32 -> 12 -> 25 -> 22 -> 21 -> 7 -> 16 -> 6 -> 33 -> 38 -> 4 -> 15 -> 5 -> 29 -> 37 -> 19 -> 2 -> 11 -> 40 -> 27 -> 9 -> 3 -> 1. The side panel shows the 20 constant-step rows d = 1..20 of K_(41, 43), each a bar of 41 cells coloured by the midpoint colour (x + y)/2 of its edges (a rainbow, since every row is a Hamilton cycle with 41 distinct leaves), the cell carrying its one A edge marked in gold and its one B edge in cyan. Asserted before drawing: A and B are perfect matchings on Z_41 minus 0 and starters, their edge sums are complementary halves of Z_41^*, A u B is one 40-cycle, and the replay fills all 41 x 43 = 1763 edges of K_(41, 43) exactly once with 64 pieces, the optimal count, which forces the multiset 43 singletons + one 80-cycle + twenty 82-cycles (1720 cycle edges over 21 cycles of length at most 82 fall exactly 2 short).
svg.text: edge k of row d joins hub kd to hub (k+1)d
cell colour = the edge's midpoint colour (x+y)/2
boxed: the row's one A edge and one B edge
the 40 displaced edges carry their midpoint colours
onto the 80-cycle A u B (the one short cycle)
(lambda, mu) = (26, 14) in C_1, g = 6, M = 8, t = 5: A = {x, 26x} on C_0 u C_2, {x, 14x} on C_4 u C_6; B likewise on C_1 u C_3, C_5 u C_7
